properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's idea, 2026-08-10, in his words: *"is there a way to assess unmade decisions as 'risk' in getting towards the projects goal? like you need to make this chain of decisions before your project can be implemented... almost like the critical path on decision making. for each project (to include reflow2), when I first do where-am-i, I get the critical path of decisions I need to make."* And the pain behind it, also his: *"I generate many many ideas and really use the brainstorm skill a lot... but I often come up with another idea before making a decision on the previous brainstorming idea. sometimes this is on purpose as I just have a thought and want it captured and I'll decide later."*

THE ANSWER MUST BE BOUNDED TO HUMAN THROUGHPUT, added by Anthony in the same conversation and it constrains every option below: *"many projects have hundreds of decisions and a person can only make a small subset of decisions a day. especially with somebody like me, I think about 25 ideas a minute (exaggerating)... having something that says, these are your top 5 priorities would be great."* SO THE OUTPUT IS A SHORT RANKED LIST, NOT A FULL ORDERING. This matters more than it sounds: a ranked list of 83 is the same as no ranking, and it is the shape the pile already has. A top-5 also changes what the ranking must be GOOD at — it need only get the head right, not the tail, which makes several of the weaker signals below usable that would be useless for a total order. It also means the cut line is a claim: whatever is at rank 6 is being said not to matter today, and that claim should be visible rather than silent.

HALF OF THIS IS ALREADY ACCEPTED INTENT AND MUST NOT BE RE-DECIDED. `req:what-next` (status ACCEPTED, his own earlier words) already says: *"The answer must rank an unmade decision ABOVE the work that waits on it, because being told to build something blocked on a choice only the human can make is worse than being told nothing."* `cap:what-next` is PLANNED, and its recorded blocker HAS EXPIRED — `cap:derived-completion` reached `verified` and the park was never revisited, which the capability itself notes with "NOBODY NOTICED". It also already wants the which-decisions-shape-everything section, with the measured caveat that raw in-degree is the wrong signal because the top hit was a pruning decision governing ten DROPPED requirements. SO THE RANKING HALF IS DESIGNED, AGREED AND UNBLOCKED. What is genuinely new here is the CHAIN, the RISK framing, the BOUND, and putting it at the FRONT of where-am-i.

MEASURED BEFORE ANY OF THIS WAS RECORDED, and it inverts the premise:

    open (proposed) decisions                                    83
    of those, governing ANYTHING at all                          22
    of those, governing NOTHING — no downstream, so NO PATH      61
    decision->decision precedence edges among open decisions     12   (mostly CONTRADICTS, not precedence)
    items scheduled into an epoch                                23
    of those, blocked by an open decision                         2

THE CRITICAL PATH IS NOT UNCOMPUTABLE FOR WANT OF AN ALGORITHM — budget.rs already runs Kahn toposort and longest-path, and `cap:bl-150` records that it is hand-rolled there and unavailable elsewhere. It is uncomputable because THREE QUARTERS OF THE PILE HAS NO SUCCESSOR. A path needs something downstream and 61 of these have nothing.

⇒ THE QUESTION THAT ACTUALLY MATTERS, and it is not the one asked: are those 61 ideas genuinely not blocking anything yet — in which case the honest answer is "your undecided pile carries almost no risk to the goal, and that is why you can safely keep deferring" — or are they blocking things the graph was never told about? THOSE TWO LOOK IDENTICAL FROM INSIDE THE GRAPH AND NEED DIFFERENT ANSWERS. Everything below is downstream of that.

THE OPTIONS.

(A) BUILD `cap:what-next` AS ALREADY DESIGNED AND STOP. It ranks the 22 that govern something, says plainly that 61 are unranked because they connect to nothing, and leaves it there. Cheapest by far; the intent is already accepted so nothing new needs deciding. WITH THE BOUND, this gets stronger: a top-5 drawn from 22 rankable items is a real answer, where a total ordering of 83 would not be. Counter: it answers "what should I decide next" only for a quarter of the pile, and the 61 are exactly the ones he feels buried by.

(B) ASK ONE QUESTION AT CAPTURE TIME — when a brainstorm is recorded, ask what it bears on, and draw that edge. Converts a musing into something rankable without deciding it. Counter, and it is the serious one: THE BRAINSTORM SKILL IS FRICTIONLESS BY DESIGN AND THAT IS WHY HE USES IT. It explicitly forbids manufacturing links, and adding a question at capture taxes the one habit that is working. It would also often be unanswerable — half-formed ideas frequently do not yet know what they bear on, which is what makes them ideas.

(C) DERIVE THE LINKAGE, ASK RATHER THAN ASSERT — use the search index to propose what an idea probably bears on, and surface it as a question at read time instead of an edge at write time. Keeps capture frictionless and fits `dec:ask-not-repair`'s standing shape (a suspicion is a DETECT gap, never a repair). Counter: similarity over prose is exactly the scoring that produced 81-85 scores on unrelated requirements (`fact:defect-merge-survivor-ignores-priority-and-status`), so the proposals would be noisy — and a noisy proposal at orientation time is the cry-wolf failure this project has now named three times.

(D) A REAL CRITICAL PATH, FOR THE 22 THAT HAVE ONE. Declare decision-to-decision precedence (DEPENDS_ON between Decisions already exists, 10 edges design-wide) and run the toposort and longest path budget.rs already implements. Counter: with 12 precedence-ish edges among open decisions, mostly CONTRADICTS, the longest chain today is likely 1-2 hops. A "critical path" of length two is a list with a promotion.

(E) RISK, SCORED RATHER THAN PATHED. Score each open decision by what it blocks — how much is GOVERNED_BY it, how deep the downstream goes, and whether any of it is SCHEDULED into an epoch. That is computable TODAY with no new edges and no new vocabulary, and a score is exactly what a top-5 needs. Counter, and it is the honest one: run it now and the answer is that risk is nearly zero, because only 2 of 23 scheduled items are blocked by an open decision. That may be true and reassuring, or it may mean the schedule is what is under-modelled rather than the decisions.

(F) THE PILE'S REAL PROBLEM MAY BE AGE, NOT BLOCKING. Rank by staleness — how long has this been open, has anything touched its region since — rather than by path. `cap:revise-trigger` already exists for surfacing a settled road worth re-opening, and `cap:what-next`'s own expired park is a worked example of a condition nobody watches. Counter: age is not importance, and a stale-first ranking would put genuinely deferred ideas above newly urgent ones.

(G) RANK BY ATTENTION RATHER THAN BY CONSEQUENCE — `dec:idea-what-gets-searched-repeatedly-is-becoming-important`, recorded separately the same day. A node the user keeps circling back to may be ripening whether or not it blocks anything. NOT A SUBSTITUTE: a decision can draw attention and block nothing, or block everything and never be searched. Whether the two compose into one ranking, or are two lists, is open in both nodes and settled in neither.

WHAT IS NOT AN OPTION: deciding things to shorten the list. Anthony said the deferral is often deliberate — *"sometimes this is on purpose"* — so a mechanism whose success is measured by the pile shrinking would be optimising against how he actually works. The bound makes this concrete: a top-5 that never changes because he keeps not deciding is working correctly, not failing.

ONE THING TO SETTLE BEFORE ANY OF THESE, because "risk to the goal" needs a goal: the Project's objective is one sentence, "keep a design coherent from concept through operations", and nothing decomposes it. Risk is currently measurable only against EPOCHS, which are the nearest thing to a target the graph holds. Whether the goal itself should be modelled is a separate question this node does not open.
properties.name: OPEN — can unmade decisions be ranked as risk to the goal, bounded to what a person can actually decide in a day, when 61 of 83 of them govern nothing and so have no path?
properties.rationale:
Anthony's idea, recorded as an open question because the measurement changed what the question is. He asked for a critical path; the graph says three quarters of the undecided pile has no successor to path through, so the prior question is whether that disconnection is true or merely unrecorded.

REVISED the same session it was created, to fold in the top-5 bound he added minutes later, rather than minting a second node. The bound is a constraint on the answer to THIS question, not a new question — and given that the complaint driving all of it is a pile of 83 open decisions, answering "how do I triage the pile" by adding another node to the pile would be a poor demonstration. Recorded without a snapshot because the node had not yet been exported or committed and both versions are this session's own capture; a fold after the record ships would need `revise-design` proper.

Kept as one node rather than several because all seven options answer the same question — how to triage undecided work — and splitting them would create a set that can only be half-answered. Options are not registered as alternatives, so `undecided_decision_point` stays quiet and the loop says nothing while this is still thinking.

No approver edge, deliberately, per the brainstorm discipline: this is thinking out loud, and attaching an approver would make `loop_status` start reporting it as owed. If it becomes a real fork — most likely between (A) and (E), which are both buildable now and compose naturally under a bound — `register_alternative` is what promotes it.

Recorded WITHOUT wiring it to `req:what-next` or `cap:what-next`. Those are cited in the text and the relationship is real, but drawing edges from a musing to accepted intent would assert that this idea shapes them, which nobody has decided. That restraint is also the subject of option (B), which makes it worth stating rather than doing silently.
